Caliber: warmup=25, repeats=10, per-case msprof capture, trailing-10 mean | 2026-09-15 case 重设（放大 shape 命中目标分档）后按本管线口径全量重测；新增 latency_band_distribution。
caliber: warmup=25, repeats=10, per-case msprof capture, trailing-10 mean; gap-fenced iteration segmentation (instrumented sync+sleep separator, floor 9 ms); convergence gate = |drift| <= 5% on mean(2nd half of last 10)/mean(1st half), judged separately for e2e and core

window_mix.note: extended_cases were re-measured ONLY after failing the convergence gate at the modal window; no case that already passed was re-rolled. paired_ab_bound_pct is the largest per-case move seen in a same-case paired A/B between the modal and the extended window (null = not established for this operator, which is NOT the same as zero).

source_annotation.assembled_source: ops-cv resize_nearest_neighbor_v2 aclnn 实测（warmup=3, repeats=3, msprof --ai-core task_time 中值）; measured impl = /home/zzy-work/cv_perf_level3/adapters/ref_20_resize_nearest.py. Caliber: warmup=25, repeats=10, per-case msprof capture, trailing-10 mean; gap-fenced iteration segmentation (instrumented sync+sleep separator, floor 9 ms); convergence gate = |drift| <= 5% on mean(2nd half of last 10)/mean(1st half), judged separately for e2e and core. MFU DENOMINATOR CHANGED (pre-delivery, 2026-09-13): all ten CV operators are now divided by the vector peak 48 x 0.2304 = 11.0592 TFLOPS (48 measured -- the framework's own Transpose kernels launch at Block Dim = 48; cross-checked against the archived profile's 'AI Core Freq 1800 MHz'), instead of the 353.8944 fp16 Cube peak used by the previously shipped 12-21 perf.json. MFU here is therefore ~32x the shipped file's. This is a caliber unification, NOT a statement that the engines are uniform -- measured per case they are not: 12/15/16/19 are pure AI_VECTOR_CORE, 13 adds MIX_AIV, 14 runs MIX_AIC on 34 of 47 cases and really occupies the Cube (cube_utilization 85-95%), and 17/18/20/21 carry AI_CPU cases that never reach an AI Core. The vector peak is exact only for the pure-AIV operators; for 14 the Cube peak is arguably closer, and for AI_CPU cases neither applies. MFU is a tie-breaker in this pipeline -- quote it with achieved_bw_gbs, never alone. Per-operator engine mix: OPT_HINTS.md. FORMAT NOTICE (added 2026-09-13): this file does NOT carry an accuracy verdict. The previously shipped 12-21 perf.json had `accuracy_passed_cases` (top level) and a per-case `accuracy`; the schema used here records `cases_valid` (a usable msprof capture was obtained) and `cases_converged` (the |drift| <= 5% gate passed) instead -- NEITHER is an accuracy statement, and neither should be read as one. Accuracy evidence exists by route and its strength is NOT uniform: for the bridge routes (12/13/14/15/16/20) `wrapper.py --check` compares the adapter against the repo Model and is a genuine comparison rather than a self-comparison; the measuring lanes REPORT max_abs_diff 0.000e+00 on the cases they sampled (REPORTED, NOT RE-VERIFIED IN THIS PASS, and this pass did not sample 12 or 16); for the pure-delegate torch routes (17/18/19/21) the same check compares the Model against itself and is TAUTOLOGICAL -- it confirms wiring and shapes only, not accuracy. Per-case `impl_latency_us` was renamed `latency_us`; same quantity, same caliber, no alias is provided, so a consumer keying on the old name must be updated. WINDOW MIX: 21 of 50 cases were re-measured on a longer window after failing the convergence gate at w25/r10 (see window_mix.extended_cases); every other case is from the modal window, and no passing case was re-rolled.
source_annotation.note: NOTE (route split, added by the 2026-09-13 cv_perf_level3 measurement): the 50 cases are NOT all the same implementation, and this is forced, not chosen. The three populations below were confirmed by reading the per-case core op name out of msprof op_summary for ALL 50 cases, not by sampling: 34/34 -> ResizeNearestNeighborV2, 12/12 -> UpsampleNearest, 4/4 -> the same torch index chain (identical op set in all four). There is NO shape/scale dispatch split inside the expressible set -- unlike 14_resize_bilinear, where the same aclnn entry splits 13/47 to ResizeBilinearV2 and 34/47 to UpsampleBilinear2d at scale==2.0. For this operator both scale==2.0 plain cases (0 and 14) land on ResizeNearestNeighborV2, so the split here is driven purely by the half_pixel_centers / align_corners attributes. Note also that this one file contains two of the three ways a 'core op' list can be multiple, and counting signatures cannot tell them apart: (a) and (b) above are a genuine DISPATCH (one entry point, different AI Core kernels, selected by the half_pixel_centers / align_corners attribute), whereas (c) is a torch DECOMPOSITION chain (generic elementwise/index kernels with no single aclnn kernel behind them). The discriminator is whether the signature contains a constant non-generic kernel: (a)/(b) each are one such kernel (with a size dispatch in 14's case); (c) has none. A third category, not present here, is a constant kernel core plus a varying optional branch (the shape 21_spatial_transformer falls into). (a) 34 cases (half_pixel_centers=False, align_corners=False): core kernel is the CANN built-in ResizeNearestNeighborV2 -- measured name, not inferred. The ops-cv vendor custom_cv_cv has NO 910b kernel for ResizeNearestNeighborV2 (it is registered only for ascend950), so the ops-cv aclnn route falls back to the built-in too; on those cases the aclnn route and this torch route are the same kernel at the same time (case0: 3.78 us aclnn vs 3.66 us torch, both ResizeNearestNeighborV2). (b) 12 cases (half_pixel_centers=True): the repo Model uses F.interpolate(mode='nearest-exact'), core kernel UpsampleNearest (class range 2.889-36.888 us, geomean 7.3381 -- not a typical value). (c) 4 cases (align_corners=True, half_pixel_centers=False): the repo Model uses its own fp32 index-gather path, which on NPU is a 7-op torch chain (Range/Mul/RealDiv/Add/Floor/ClipByValueV2/Index, ~15 kernel launches/iter). Its cost is NOT launch overhead as one might assume: measured per-op on bare captures (median of 35 iterations), a single Index op on AI_CPU dominates -- case 4: Index AI_CPU 213.609 of 226.820 us core = 94.2% (per-op medians over 35 iterations; cases 30 and 35 measured the same way) -- all three AICPU cases measured, not inferred. ENGINE-EVIDENCE PROVENANCE: those per-operator AI_CPU/AI_VECTOR_CORE splits are SELF-MEASURED from bare op_summary captures (raw PROF trees retained under out/_probe/keep20_acT, keep20_acT30, keep20_c35), NOT read from a field of this file. At the time of writing, this file carried no per-case engine/task_type key, so grep-ing it for AI_CPU only hits this sentence -- but if a later revision exposes a field for these quantities, prefer that field and treat this note as superseded. So for 3 of these 4 cases (4/30/35) core_us is ~90%+ HOST CPU time, not AI Core time, and none of it is a resize kernel. Case 40 is the exception that proves the point: there the SAME Index op runs on AI_VECTOR_CORE (6.240 us) and the AICPU share is 0% -- i.e. one core op NAME can be dispatched to different ENGINES in different cases, so task_type has to be read per case and cannot be inferred from the op name. By contrast all 46 plain + hpc=True cases run wholly on AI_VECTOR_CORE.No single-op route exists on this box for (b)/(c): aclnnUpsampleNearest2d/V2 carries no half_pixel_centers or align_corners argument (vendor header aclnn_upsample_nearest_2d_v2.h), and the aclop path that could reach the built-in op's own two bool attributes is dead in CANN 8.5.1 (aclopCompileAndExecuteV2 is not exported; aclopExecuteV2 returns Inner Error 100024). CONSEQUENCE: the 50-case geomean is pulled up by the 4 index-chain cases -- and for 3 of them that number is host CPU time, so it must not enter an AI-Core-utilization comparison either. A subset PER-CLASS MEASURED SPREAD (n / core_us range / geomean) -- the geomeans are the comparable figures, but the ranges are 13-40x wide, so quoting a single typical value for a class would mislead: plain n=34 / 1.724-36.204 / 4.7118 us; hpc=True n=12 / 2.889-36.888 / 7.3381 us; ac=True n=4 / 31.673-235.307 / 117.2098 us. geomean over the 34 genuine single-kernel ResizeNearestNeighborV2 cases (all AI_VECTOR_CORE) is recorded in geomean_subsets for sideways comparison with 12-17. WINDOW/RE-MEASURE PROVENANCE (window_mix.note is auto-generated and understates this): of the 21 cases whose value comes from an extended window, only 5 (1/5/21/31/36) were re-measured for failing the convergence gate; the other 16 (the hpc/ac cases 3/4/8/16/23/24/25/29/30/33/35/37/40/41/45/49) were re-measured because their first capture VOIDed with 'no op_summary csv' -- a transient cross-lane interference in which all 16 failed in two separate batches while every one of the 34 plain cases passed, yet each succeeded on individual re-run. So the extended-window set here mixes two different reasons, and the 16 are re-runs of cases that had NO valid first measurement at all. CASE 16 and CASE 36 carry status=not_converged: their residual drift is -10.3% and -10.0% against the |drift|<=5% gate, but this is measurement noise, not a remaining ramp. Their tail window means are stationary to 0.2% (case16: 15.546/15.521/15.550 us) and 3.8% (case36: 4.346/4.292/4.454 us), their core values are stable across three independent windows (case36: 4.382/4.600/4.393 us at w25/r10, w50/r20, w80/r40), and their drift SIGN FLIPS between runs (case36: +5.6%, +14.4%, -10.0%). Note the gate is computed on the last 10 iterations only, whatever warmup/repeats are, so extending the window cannot rescue a noisy case -- it only helps a genuine slow ramp. The reported values are the tail means. PEAK NOTE (measured engines), REWRITTEN 2026-09-13: every kernel this operator runs was observed on AI_VECTOR_CORE or AI_CPU -- none on Cube. As of the 2026-09-13 caliber unification this file carries the VECTOR peak 11.0592 TFLOPS (all ten operators were switched; see MFU DENOMINATOR CHANGED), which is the right denominator for its AI_VECTOR_CORE part. SUPERSESSION: an earlier version of this note said the vector peak 'would be' right and that the shipped field was the Cube peak -- that was true before the unification and is not any more. MFU IS DELIBERATELY NOT EMITTED: this operator is registered BYTES ONLY (`flops_20_resize_nearest`, method='bytes_only'), so `mfu_pct`/`mfu_pct_legacy` are null BY DESIGN, not because a formula is missing. Reasons (see that entry's own note): no validated analytic FLOPs model, and an engine mix that is not single-peaked (47 pure AI_VECTOR_CORE + 3 AI_CPU), so no single peak denominator applies to the file. `bytes_moved` IS emitted, is ALGORITHMIC in/out only, is a STRICT LOWER BOUND for this chain-shaped operator, and is NOT comparable with single-kernel operators; the max over cases is an UPPER BOUND on a rate, not a rate. The defensible evidence that no single value can represent this operator is MODEL-FREE, from the case specs: input elements 9 -> 4194304 (= 466034x), output elements 1 -> 3145728 (= 3145728x). AI_CPU CONTAMINATION (added 2026-09-13 by the consolidation pass). The machine-readable form of this is the per-case `engines` / `has_aicpu` fields, which ARE fields of this file -- key any decision on those, not on the percentage below. The percentage is MEASURED BY HAND and is NOT a field: this pass recomputed the same captures (paths above; case 40 = 0.0%, see the case-40 exception earlier) and got 98.3% for case 4 over all iterations versus 89.8% over the trailing 10 -- the same measurement as the per-op figure above under a different convention. The AI_CPU percentages in this note are therefore NOT additive and none of them alone is the operator's value. DEFINITION-DEPENDENT, and this pass could not reconcile the lanes' conventions: recomputing from the same kept captures moves the figure materially, because BOTH the row window AND whether the glue set (Transpose/TransData/Cast/MemSet/ZerosLike/ViewCopy) is stripped change the denominator. Quote it with its convention or not at all. CONSEQUENCE regardless of the exact number: core_us for the flagged cases is partly HOST CPU time, so those cases must NOT enter an AI-Core-utilization comparison, and an optimization aimed at AI Core work cannot reach that part of the time.
